tagline: The old river crossing curves toward a dam bypassed by traffic.
intro: Hoover Dam Road follows the old US 93 alignment along a curving mountainside over Rough Summit. SR 172 provides the approach from I-11/US 93, passing the turnoff for the Lakeview scenic viewpoint before its designation ends just short of the dam reservation’s security checkpoint. The entire state route lies within Lake Mead National Recreation Area, whose protected landscape includes the reservoir and surrounding desert terrain.

The dam’s crest once carried US 93 across the Colorado River. Through traffic mixed with walkers and dam visitors, producing congestion on the crossing and its approaches. The old approaches had hairpin turns on both sides of the river, with terrain limiting sightlines through curves. Officials had discussed an alternative crossing since the 1960s. The bypass opened on October 19, 2010, moving US 93 to a new crossing and leaving SR 172 on the old alignment.

From the interstate interchange, turn onto the old Nevada Highway and continue east over Rough Summit toward Lakeview. Beyond the checkpoint, the access road passes the memorial bridge plaza and visitor center, then crosses the dam into Arizona. The public drive loops through a parking area and returns the way it came. At the bridge, stairs and ramps connect the Nevada parking area to the pedestrian sidewalk.

moments.title: Lakeview turnoff
moments.text: The turnoff for the Lakeview scenic viewpoint comes after Rough Summit on the eastbound approach to Hoover Dam. Just beyond it, SR 172 ends before the reservation’s security checkpoint. The road itself continues as Hoover Dam Access Road, carrying visitors toward the bridge plaza and dam.

moments.title: Mike O'Callaghan-Pat Tillman Memorial Bridge
moments.text: The bridge that took US 93 off the dam opened in 2010, removing hairpin turns and blind curves from the highway’s route. Its concrete arch and columns support a steel roadway deck, a combination chosen to control cost and schedule while complementing the dam. The name honors Nevada governor Mike O’Callaghan and Pat Tillman, who left professional football for the Army and was killed by friendly fire in Afghanistan. The distinction for visitors is between driving and walking: the dam is not visible from vehicles crossing the bridge, but its sidewalk provides views of the dam and river.

moments.title: Hoover Dam
moments.text: Hoover Dam’s curved concrete face transfers the force of the stored water into the canyon walls. Six Companies began construction in 1931, and the federal government accepted the dam in March 1936, more than two years ahead of schedule. The concrete was poured in blocks with cooling pipes inside them; after each block stopped contracting, workers filled the pipes with grout. Architect Gordon B. Kaufmann gave the project its Art Deco treatment, including turrets rising from the dam face and clocks on the intake towers. Two traffic lanes cross the top, where US 93 formerly crossed the river.

practical: Hoover Dam: Approach from Nevada and return to Nevada after crossing the dam; through traffic is not allowed. Some vehicles cannot cross the dam. (checked 2026-10-11)
